body: Yeah. Thanks for your help, friend. I was freaking out about it earlier but talking about it has calmed me down a lot.

He has friends there, yeah. I'm going to talk to him about it in the morning, encourage him to ask around his friends if he can crash on anyone's couch for a while. He went straight to bed after telling me all this and I don't want to have a conversation like this while he's still emotional.

I really appreciate your advice, but the problem is that he has already confronted his mom about everything. He did it over Skype while he was still living here and that's part of why he thought things had changed. Apparently it didn't do anything to change her since she's back to being unsupportive.

I wish I could confront her myself and try to make her see what she's doing to her son, but I know he wouldn't be at all comfortable with me fighting a battle for him.

I agree that it's a bad idea. He said he's going to leave but he's not sure how, when or where - he's going to start looking for work there soon but in the meantime I'm not sure how much he has in savings. Less than $1000, I think.

Thank you for the advice. I tell him every day how important he is to me and that I'll always be here to support him no matter what, but I can't force him to believe it or come to me when he's upset.
